messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: quick marginal question
parts:
Hi,

mean(s.eff > 0), where s.eff is sampled Fromm the posterior distribution, estimates the probability p that s.eff > 0. That means that p corresponds to the upper quantile 0. Thus, inla.pmarginal for quantile 0 will give you 1-p.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: quick marginal question
parts:
Hi,

0.96985 is less than 0.975, which is the lower 2.5% quantile -0.0012
shown in the table, which forms the lower point of a two-sided 95%
interval.
A one-sided one-sided interval that ends at +infinity needs to start
at a point to the right of -0.0012 to cover the same probability mass;
in this case that takes the left endpoint above 0. The extra
probability from 0.95 to 0.96985 is the probability mass between 0 and
the left endpoint of the one-sided interval.
So yes, 1-pmarginal is the probability of exceeding 0.

Finn
